description.narrative: The objective of the Uttarakhand Disaster Recovery Project for India is to restore housing, rural connectivity and build resilience of communities in Uttarakhand and increase the technical capacity of the state entities to respond promptly and effectively to an eligible crisis or emergency. There are six components to the project, the first component being resilient infrastructure reconstruction. The objective of this component is to focus on the immediate needs of reconstruction of damaged houses and public buildings. The aim is to reduce the vulnerability of the affected population and restore access to the basic services of governance. The second component is the rural road connectivity. The objective of this component is to restore the connectivity lost due to the disaster through the reconstruction of damaged roads and bridges including: village roads, Other District Roads (ODRs), bridle roads and bridle bridges. The third component is the technical assistance and capacity building for disaster risk management. The objective of this component is to enhance the capabilities of government entities and others in risk mitigation and response. The fourth component is the financing disaster response expenses. This component will support the financing of eligible expenses already incurred by the state during the immediate post-disaster response period. The fifth component is the implementation support. This component will support the incremental operating costs of the project, including the operation of the Project Management Unit (PMU) and the respective Project Implementation Units (PIUs). Finally, the sixth component is the contingency emergency response.

To restore housing, rural connectivity and build resilience of communities in Uttarakhand and increase the technical capacity of the State entities to respond promptly and effectively to an eligible crisis or emergency.

Finance Agreement :Screening of Activities Government Permits/Clearance, Social & Environmental Doc | Description :Prior tocommencement of any civil works Uttarakhand shall ensure (i) all relevant government permits/clearances have been obtained& met(ii) respective activities are screened as per the ESMF & whenever required the necessary EMP, RAP, social management plans havebeen prepared & disclosed; (iii) resettlement measures identified have been properly implemented includ. resettlement compensation.| Frequency :CONTINUOUS

To access funds under this component, the Recipient and the Project Implementing Entity must have determined/declared that aneligible crisis or emergency has occurred, identified response activities and expenditures, prepared and disclosed any requiredsafeguard documents, identified and/or staffed a coordination authority responsible for implementation, and prepared an operationsmanual.

Uttarakhand shall (i) maintain monitoring and evaluation protocols and record keeping procedures to supervise and assess compliancewith Safeguard Documents; and (ii) to report on quarterly basis on compliance with Safeguard Documents.

Uttarakhand shall ensure that, prior to commencement of any civil works: (i) all relevant government permits/clearances have beenobtained, and/or any conditions imposed have been fulfilled/met; (ii) the respective activities have been screened as per the ESMFand, whenever required the necessary Environment Management Plan, Resettlement Management Plan, Social Management Plans have beenprepared and disclosed; and (iii) all resettlement measures identified have been properly implemented (including full payment ofany resettlement compensation).

Uttarakhand shall establish and monthly update a procurement documentation and record keeping system with a freely and publiclyaccessible database, showing updated procurement information (i.e. notices, bidding invitations, request for proposals, awards,etc.).

Uttarakhand shall implement the Project in accordance with the Operations Manuals, the Safeguard Documents (ESMF or mitigationplans derived therefrom) and the Governance and Accountability Action Plan.
Uttarakhand shall include compliance with the Safeguard Documents as part of the contractors obligations pursuant to the biddingdocuments.

Uttarakhand shall maintain: (i) the Core Committee; (ii) the High Powered Committee for Sanctions of Post Disaster ReconstructionWorks; (iii) the Project Management Unit (within USDMA); and (iv) the Project Implementation Units (the line departments andagencies); and (iv) the District level Coordination Units.
Uttarakhand shall submit to the Bank a compilation of the safeguards screening reports prepared by the line department and agencieson Project activities.

Uttarakhand to maintain an mechanism for handling procurement complaints with a second tier appeal system and complaint databaseproviding free and public access for the submission of electronic claims.

comment.narrative: <p>The initial target for this IRI was 3,600km of mostly village roads. During the first year of implementation, it was agreed that the State would finance village roads and bridle roads with their own funds because these works were simpler with relatively lowernit cost. As a result, it was decided for the sub-component to finance other district roads which are more technically complex with higher unit costs and that the scope would be reduced. This was formally revised as part of AF restructuring on November 2019. In adition, the roads incorporated improved design standards, protection infrastructure, and road safety measures which are now being widely adopted by roads built beyond the Project scope in the State.</p>

title.narrative: Depts. that make effective use of information generated by USDMA

comment.narrative: <p>The departments using USDMA data include the Planning Department, all Development Authorities (Nagar Nigam & Nagar Palika), Public Works Department (PWD), Irrigation Department, Agriculture and Horticulture Department, Uttarakhand State Disaster Management Authority (USDMA) in conjunction with District Disaster Management Authorities (DDMAs) for emergency operations, and the Power Departments (Uttarakhand Power Corporation Ltd. - UPCL, Uttarakhand Jal Vidyut Nigam Ltd - UJVNL, and Power Transmission Corporatio of Uttarakhand Ltd - PTCUL). Other departments are the Water Department, Police Department, State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), Department of Industries, Tourism Department, Transport Corporation, Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority (UCADA), Department of Telecom (DoT), Medical and Health Department, Geological Survey of India (GSI), and the Information Technology Development Agency (ITDA). Apart from this, the data were given to Indian Institute of Remote Sensing (IIRS) Dehradun (under a joint MoU) and National Disaster Risk Management Authority.</p>

title.narrative: Number of bridges built or restored

comment.narrative: <p>Initially, this IRI was "Number of bridle bridges restored" which was revised as "Number of bridges built and restored" and the target was revised from 140 to 88 which covered both restored bridges and new bridges under the Project - 24 bridges under the Parent Project and 64 bridges under the Additional Financing portion. Further, through the October 2020 restructuring, number of bridges was revised from 88 to 79 owing to reallocation due to CERC component becoming activated. Finally, the project has completed 81 bridges, the number of bridges exceeds the target of 79.</p>

Targeted affected HHs with multi-hazard resilient housing

comment.narrative: The original indicators and targets were established with limited information in the aftermath of the June 2013 disaster. As this was an emergency operation, the full project scope and details were not known at the time of project preparation. All damage and recovery estimates were based on the August 2013 Joint Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment Report and the project was approved by the Board four months after the disaster. During implementation, the final scope and unit costs were revised. This activity was financed under the original IDA Credit and closed. Despite not achieving 100 percent of the 2,500 targeted houses, more than 95 percent is considered a very successful outcome for an innovative owner-driven construction process.
